main_body: T-shaped timber post: a horizontal crossbeam (rows 9-17) on top of a thin vertical post (rows 18-47)
top_band: Rows 10-12 orange (L=157) then a cream highlight row 13 (L=239); the orange is only 3 rows and sits directly above a same-family brown face (rows 14-15). The whole beam is a flat front-facing bar, and the post below has no top surface at all.
evidence: The crossbeam is a thin horizontal bar of about 9 rows with a 3-row orange band, a cream edge line, and a 2-row brown face with a dark underside. It reads as a front-elevation bar rather than a beam with a real top face. The post is a 3-4 px wide vertical strip drawn straight from the front, with no horizontal surface and no base showing a top. For a frame, the beams and base must show top faces. The base is missing, and the post ends in an outline row. The overall object is a flat T silhouette that does not satisfy the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours against 38-40 for the references. The median colours per tile is 0 because the piece is narrow. The post is a long strip of one flat brown (rows 22-45) with no grain or texture dots, which counts as a flat fill despite the measured 0% coverage, since the strip is only about 3 px wide. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral), which is fine. The beam has a few highlight and dither pixels, but overall the piece is far thinner and flatter than the roofed well and the stall, so it would look noticeably poorer next to them.
